Co-founder Moritz Fürste said after the event that organisers “made a mistake by not reacting immediately during the race”.New rules have since been introduced to give race organisers the power to remove an athlete if their “blood, vomit, urine, or faeces poses a welfare or contamination risk to the racer or to other racers”.Rules were already in place to penalise athletes for minor infractions such as littering on the course, or spitting or clearing their nose on the floor.Wietrzyk was subjected to vitriol when her identity was shared online following the incident in Beijing, prompting Hyrox organisers to warn that anyone sending abuse or threats of violence towards the athlete would be banned from future events.Explore more on these topicsAustralia sportFitnessnewsShareReuse this content

title: Michael Carrick insists he will still be in charge of Manchester United against Roma | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Michael Carrick has insisted he will still be in charge when Manchester United face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday despite the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Michael Carrick has insisted he will still be in charge when Manchester United face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday despite the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea
Content: Michael Carrick said ‘I’m just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek.’Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick said ‘I’m just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek.’Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianManchester UnitedMichael Carrick insists he will still be in charge of Manchester United against RomaDefeat against Chelsea extends winless run to nine gamesCarrick clinging on to job after club’s worst run since 1988Jacob Steinbergat Stamford BridgeSat 31 Oct 2026 12.43 EDTLast modified on Sat 31 Oct 2026 17.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick insisted he would still be in charge when Manchester United face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday, despite the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday. United’s problems mounted as theirwinless run reached nine games. Carrick is clinging on to his job after overseeing the club’s first such run since 1988 and tried to focus on the next game as he analysed his side’s defending when Morgan Rogers opened the scoring for Chelsea.“It’s never a good goal to concede,” he said. “Morgan went through the middle of us and at that point the game was right in the balance. To concede like that was a big moment. I’m just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek now.”Manchester United crisis deepens with Chelsea defeat and Martínez red cardRead moreUnited played well during the first half, but missed a series of clear opportunities. They folded after going behind and their fate was sealed when Lisandro Martínez was sent off for a foul that led to Cole Palmer making it 2-0 from the spot. Carrick, though, steered clear of criticising one of his most experienced players for leaving United in the lurch.“It was a major part of the game,” he said. “The second goal and losing the man at that stage had a big influence on it.”United were just above the bottom three before the afternoon games, but Carrick said there would be no stigma attached to one of the biggest clubs in the country falling into the relegation zone should results elsewhere have that effect. “There’s no words I’m going to explain to you now that makes it any different,” he said. “It’s not going to change it. We’ve got to move forward and win matches, it’s as simple as that.”View image in fullscreenLisandro Martínez isn’t looking at his man when he barges into Wesley Fofana, giving away a penalty, and earning a red card in the process.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianCarrick was asked if his players were ready for a relegation battle. “You can look at it like that, and you can look at how far you can move up the league quite quickly if you win football matches,” he said. “That’s the way it’s got to be approached.”Chelsea moved into fourth place overnight, respondingwell to losing to Tottenhamin the league andLiverpool on penaltiesin the Carabao Cup. “The first half was intense,” Xabi Alonso said. “United had their chances, we were close as well, so at half-time we have spoken and the reaction from the second half was better.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“We started quite well, we got the lead, we looked in better control and after 2-0 and the red card the context of the game changed. But it has not been easy.”Alonso praised Estêvão Willian after the Brazil winger sparkled on his first start in the league this season. “We spoke after Tottenham and he knew that he was going to be playing today,” theChelseamanager said. “He has had the best response to show he deserves more, that he was prepared and that’s what you want, so I’m very happy for him.”Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarrickChelseanewsShareReuse this content

title: Zion Suzuki horror own goal haunts Aston Villa to hand Fulham a point | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Zion Suzuki’s second-half own goal gave Fulham an equaliser in their 1-1 draw at Aston Villa to cancel out Nicolas Jackson’s opener
Author: Peter Lansley
Headline: Zion Suzuki’s second-half own goal gave Fulham an equaliser in their 1-1 draw at Aston Villa to cancel out Nicolas Jackson’s opener
Content: Zion Suzuki carries the ball over his own line to hand Fulham their equalising goal.Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenZion Suzuki carries the ball over his own line to hand Fulham their equalising goal.Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/ReutersPremier LeagueZion Suzuki horror own goal haunts Aston Villa to hand Fulham a pointPeter Lansleyat Villa ParkSat 31 Oct 2026 18.15 EDTLast modified on Sat 31 Oct 2026 19.44 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFulham helped cement Jamie Carragher’s argument thatAston Villawill never be Manchester United. No, they know how to grind out a point on a bad day and can go to Barcelona on Tuesday with some confidence.Villa’s goalkeeper Zion Suzuki dropped Alex Iwobi’s corner over his own goalline to deny Unai Emery’s team a fifth win in six games after Nicolas Jackson’s eighth goal of the season had promised to lift a resurgent Villa back into the top third of thePremier League. Not even John McGinn’s missed penalty had looked set to deny them as they took control in the first period.Julio Enciso strikes again to earn Ipswich a point against HullRead moreBut while Villa were made to look below par by aFulhamside making it seven points from the last nine, the home supporters sang long and loud to make their manager know how much he is appreciated.The Holte End had not waited long to voice their verdict on the spat betweenthe former England internationaland the Villa chair.Carragher had admitted that his words were “clumsy and wrong” after telling Villa fans “to shut the fuck up” as they reacted angrily to his claims that Emery should want to manage Manchester United if Michael Carrick were to be sacked after their long winless run. It seemed like a storm in a teacup to many until Nassef Sawiris issued a statement promising to initiate legal action. “As custodians of this great club, we cannot stand still while the F word is directed at Villa fans,” Sawiris said.Notwithstanding this disappointing draw, it is beyond question that Emery has done an admirable job at Villa. Even after losing another tranche of top talent, with Ollie Watkins, Morgan Rogers and Emi Martínez heading up the exits last summer afterwinning the Europa League, the former Arsenal and PSG manager has resurrected the club’s fortunes yet again. They start seasons slowly – winning only two of their last 12 league games in August and September – but once he has cast his spell and integrated the new signings, Villa tend to get going; they had won eight of their previous 10 league games in October and November.View image in fullscreenZion Suzuki fumbles the ball into the net to gift Fulham their goal.Photograph: Manjit Narotra/ProSports/ShutterstockIt must be galling to qualify for the Champions League twice in three years and yet still have your best talents lured away. So the idea that United could, in Carragher’s eyes, come and click their fingers and expect Emery to be unable to resist their faded grandeur evidently stuck in the throats of Villa fans and chair alike.Fulham’s second-half showing, in particular, merited a draw that followed their recent league wins over Hull and Coventry and kept them two points above the relegation zone in Álvaro Arbeloa’s first autumn in charge. Emery would never countenance it but perhaps Villa’s ultimate glamour trip, to Barcelona, on Tuesday before next Sunday’s visit to Old Trafford, of all places, overshadowed this game.McGinn spurned his first penalty for the club (excluding shootouts), awarded after Sander Berge was belatedly adjudged to have handled Leon Goretzka’s header, when he thundered his spot-kick against the crossbar.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenNicolas Jackson opens the scoring for Aston Villa in the first half.Photograph: Joe Giddens/PABut while Fulham had plenty of the ball, Villa appeared content to threaten on the counterattack. Indeed, they took the lead in the 39th minute after Jackson was sent running down the inside-left channel by a perfect through ball from Johan Manzambi. The £65m striker weaved into the penalty area past Timothy Castagne and David Affengruber before slotting in his fifth goal in five Premier League games.Fulham were much more dominant in the second half. “They were more aggressive than us in the first half,” Arbeloa admitted. “I told my players I know we are a team that wants to control the game through the ball. But this is the Premier League. If you want to win a game, you need to fight for every ball.” When Castagne headed on Alex Iwobi’s corner, both Gonzalo García and Shea Charles got a touch on the ball before it spooned up on to the roof of the net. Villa were riding their luck.Fulham’s dominance paid off, however, in the most unexpected fashion midway through the second half. Suzuki, who has been lauded for his early-season form, had just saved a header from Iwobi when, from the Nigerian’s ensuing corner, under no pressure, he inexplicably dropped the ball just over the line. “It’s part of football,” Emery said. “I make mistakes as coach. The players are making every match mistakes … when it’s the keeper, those mistakes are more in focus. I prefer to speak about the saves he did today.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueAston VillaFulhammatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Enzo Maresca rues ‘silly’ errors after Manchester City defeat against Brighton | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Enzo Maresca said ‘silly goals’ and individual errors are costing Manchester City after their home defeat against Brighton
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Enzo Maresca said ‘silly goals’ and individual errors are costing Manchester City after their home defeat against Brighton
Content: Enzo Maresca’s team have lost their last two league matches.Photograph: Matt McNulty/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEnzo Maresca’s team have lost their last two league matches.Photograph: Matt McNulty/Getty ImagesManchester CityEnzo Maresca rues ‘silly’ errors after Manchester City defeat against BrightonMatheus Nunes mistake lets in Yasin Ayari for winnerMaresca: ‘We are conceding silly goals that we can avoid’Jamie Jacksonat the Etihad StadiumSat 31 Oct 2026 14.38 EDTLast modified on Sat 31 Oct 2026 15.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEnzo Maresca said “silly goals” and individual errors are costing Manchester City after Matheus Nunes’ mistake allowed Yasin Ayari to scoreBrighton’s winner in Saturday’s 1-0 victoryhere. Ayari’s strike was made possible after Nunes, City’s right-back, missed Diego Gómez’s cross from the right, so the ball could come back across goal via Maxim De Cuyper.The2-1 loss at Aston Villacame from Gianluigi Donnarumma allowing Nicolas Jackson’s long-range winner to squeeze under his body.Ayari on target as Brighton stun Manchester City to close gap on leadersRead more“Sometimes it happens,” said Maresca. “Unfortunately, it is happening for our players, but it is part of football, it happens many times against us, we need to analyse, understand what we can do better and try to move on.“We are the second team in terms of scoring in the Premier League, but we are conceding silly goals that we can avoid and hopefully we can avoid in the next game.“It is a very similar feeling we had after the Aston Villa game – unfortunately we created enough to get some points but we didn’t score. At the moment it is like this. We did enough to deserve something. We need to move on and try to win games. For sure we are not happy.”While Maresca said he had not seen the free-kick awarded against Elliot Anderson to decide if this was fair, Brighton’s victory takes them to 19 points, two behind City, who are the leaders before Arsenal’s trip to Liverpool on Sunday.Fabian Hürzeler was delighted his players had changed the feeling ofWednesday’s Carabao Cup penalty shootout lossto City. “Every morning you can wake up and decide if you’re disappointed by something you cannot change or set the tone,” he said. “Stand up and have the belief that you’ll have a different feeling. It was brutal [the cup defeat]. We promised ourselves that we won’t have the same feeling.“We want to be satisfied. We created energy, positivity, the next day. You need this. We saw Saturday as an opportunity to come back stronger. This was the approach and how the players stuck together and built the connection through the four days is really impressive.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHürzeler was asked what is possible for Brighton this season. “The only thing we’re focused on is that we are in a big process, a process of analysing the game. Then try to prepare for Getafe [on Thursday], a big challenge.”Explore more on these topicsManchester CityEnzo MarescaBrighton & Hove AlbionnewsShareReuse this content

title: European football: Kane misses penalty as Dortmund share spoils in Der Klassiker | European club football | The Guardian
description: The Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane missed a penalty and hit the post for ⁠Bayern Munich as Borussia Dortmund snatched a last-gasp equaliser through Fabio Silva for a 2-2 draw ⁠in the Klassiker
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane missed a penalty and hit the post for ⁠Bayern Munich as Borussia Dortmund snatched a last-gasp equaliser through Fabio Silva for a 2-2 draw ⁠in the Klassiker
Content: Bayern Munich's Harry Kane looks rueful at the final whistle after Dortmund’s late equaliser.Photograph: Angelika Warmuth/ReutersView image in fullscreenBayern Munich's Harry Kane looks rueful at the final whistle after Dortmund’s late equaliser.Photograph: Angelika Warmuth/ReutersEuropean club footballEuropean football: Kane misses penalty as Dortmund share spoils in Der KlassikerBayern Munich held to 2-2 draw after Silva equaliserBarcelona on top of La Liga after thrashng AlavesAgenciesSat 31 Oct 2026 18.41 EDTFirst published on Sat 31 Oct 2026 16.06 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane missed a penalty and hit the post for ⁠Bayern MunichasBorussia Dortmundsnatched a last-gasp equaliser through Fabio Silva for a 2-2 draw ⁠in Der Klassiker on ⁠Saturday ​that kept the teams level on points at the top.Kane, who collected his prize in a ceremony ⁠in London on Monday, was an unused substitute in the 6-1 German Cup second-round demolition of Magdeburg on Wednesday ⁠but returned to the starting lineup on Saturday, missing from the spot with Bayern 1-0 up. He also hit ​the post, one of four ‌times Bayern struck ‌the woodwork. Silva snatched the equaliser in the 89th minute to leave both ‌teams on 18 points, with Bayern top on goal difference.In a rollercoaster first half Bayern hit the post through Michael Olise and Ismael Saibari missed a golden chance before the visitors had a goal ruled out by VAR.View image in fullscreenFabio Silva’s late equaliser keeps Dortmund level on points with Bayern at the top.Photograph: Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesBayern, ‌also hit by injuries to Serge Gnabry and Olise, struck in the 38th minute thanks to Konrad Laimer’s goal on ​the rebound, after his first effort was blocked by Dortmund’s Gregor Kobel.With the Bayern head coach, Vincent Kompany, recovering after his collapse last week, Bayern’s full-back Laimer was more threatening than Kane, who sent his 56th ⁠minute spot-kick against the crossbar. Dortmund scored through Serhou Guirassy on ​the hour but parity lasted only ​six minutes as Dayot Upamecano tapped in from a Kane ​assist from close ‌range.Kane’s low shot ​bounced off ​the post before Silva scored the equaliser. Bayern’s Lennart Karl still had time to see his shot in stoppage time bounce off the crossbar and cap a frustrating day for the champions.Elsewhere in theBundesliga, last season’s Europa League finalistsFreiburgbeatAugsburg2-1 thanks to Cyriaque Irié’s 85th-minute goal to stay third.RB Leipzigare close behind in fourth after beatingSchalke2-0. The league top scorer, Niclas Füllkrug, added his ninth goal asWerder BremenbeatHoffenheim2-0 to move up to fifth.Bayer Leverkusen’s strong early form hit another setback in a 4-2 loss at home toStuttgartfor back-to-back defeats.Borussia MönchengladbachandPaderborndrew 0-0.View image in fullscreenAtlético Madrid’s Alex Grimaldo (right) celebrates after opening the scoring against Levante.Photograph: Kai Forsterling/EPAIn Spain,Barcelonaenjoyed an emphatic 6-1 home win overAlaves, with Raphinha, Fermín López, Lamine ⁠Yamal and Anthony Gordon all on the scoresheet, as the hosts responded after losses to Real Madrid and Paris St Germain.Barcelona⁠top La Liga on 30 ⁠points, two ​ahead ofAtlético Madrid, who beatLevante2-0 earlier on Saturday, with Real Madrid six points off the pace before ⁠visiting Racing Santander on Sunday.The opening exchanges at Camp Nou were punctuated by frustrated shouts from the home manager, Hansi Flick, in response to ⁠Barcelona’s defending, butAlavessoon found it impossible to live with their fluid attacking play.“It was a hard week for us, there was no better place than Camp Nou in front of our fans [to bounce back],” López said. “They make the difference, Lamine and Raphinha, with them we will achieve big things.”There was a minute’s silence at the start of each of the day’s matches in memory of the 69 victims of thetrain crash in the province of Toledo.In Italy,Milan’s Diego Moreira claimed one goal and two assists as his side took three precious points with a 3-1 victory overInterin theirSerie Aderby on Saturday, whileRomaenjoyed a 5-2 victory at ⁠Udinese.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIn a week when ⁠the clubs ​sharedmore details of San Siro’s replacement, Milan’s fast start earned the win that lifts them into fourth ⁠place, four points behind leaders Lazio and Inter who have 25. The result means Lazio can move three points clear of Inter when they host Cagliari on Sunday. Roma ⁠are third on 24 points.Milan made the perfect start as Christian Pulisic headed their opener after four minutes ​before Adrien Rabiot added a second six minutes ‌later. Inter pulled a goal ‌back through Alessandro Bastoni in the 22nd and the momentum was with them.View image in fullscreenMilan players congratulate Diego Moreira after his goal against Inter.Photograph: Claudio Villa/AC Milan/Getty ImagesThe next goal was always ‌going to be crucial and it went to Milan as Moreira scored with a superb free-kick just before half-time to help his side to a fourth straight win over Inter.Roma were 4-0 up in 37 minutes at Udinese as they overwhelmed the hosts, who are second-bottom on five points. Bryan Cristante headed the first goal after 10 minutes, before Matías Soulé and Donyell Malen struck the woodwork. Rodrigo Mora ‌netted the second in the 31st minute after being set up by Cristante, and two minutes later Malen scored his eighth Serie A goal of the season.Evan Ndicka ​headed the fourth from a corner before half-time after which Udinese mounted something of a comeback. Nicolò Zaniolo and Matteo Palma scored for the hosts but Daniele Ghilardi added a fifth, his first Serie A goal, for Roma.Bolognaclimbed to ninth with ​a third successive league win thanks ​to a 2-1 victory overMonza, their first home success since April. Tommaso Pobega and ​Federico Bernardeschi netted for ‌Bologna, after the ​visitors scored an early ​penalty through Gustavo Varela, the top Serie A scorer with nine goals in as many games. He had been substituted by the time Monza were awarded a second penalty in the final 10 minutes and this time Patrick Cutrone missed from the spot as they were denied a point.Explore more on these topicsEuropean club footballBundesligaHarry KaneBayern MunichBorussia DortmundSerie AInternazionalenewsShareReuse this content

title: Naderi breaks Aberdeen’s resistance as Rangers reach Premier Sports Cup final | Scottish League Cup | The Guardian
description: Ryan Naderi’s late goal earned Rangers a 1-0 win against Aberdeen in the semi-final of the Premier Sports Cup at Hampden Park
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Ryan Naderi’s late goal earned Rangers a 1-0 win against Aberdeen in the semi-final of the Premier Sports Cup at Hampden Park
Content: Ryan Naderi toasts Rangers’ victory against Aberdeen which was sealed by his late goal.Photograph: Jamie Johnston/Focus Images Ltd/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenRyan Naderi toasts Rangers’ victory against Aberdeen which was sealed by his late goal.Photograph: Jamie Johnston/Focus Images Ltd/ShutterstockScottish League CupNaderi breaks Aberdeen’s resistance as Rangers reach Premier Sports Cup finalPress AssociationSat 31 Oct 2026 16.36 EDTLast modified on Sat 31 Oct 2026 18.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRyan Naderi’s dramatic late strike broke down Aberdeen’s stubborn resistance to earn Rangers a place in the Premier Sports Cup final.Aberdeen restrictedRangersto one shot on target in a low quality first half, but Derek McInnes’s side picked up the pace after the break. Aberdeen survived relentless pressure at times but in the 83rd minute Naderi redirected a strike from James Penrice into the net for his eighth goal of the season to seal a 1-0 win at Hampden Park.Scottish Premiership makes first UK move to remove Saturday 3pm broadcast blackoutRead moreThe 23-year-old Naderi later tried to share the glory, saying: “It feels amazing. I’m happy, of course, happy to be the one who scores the goals, but happy for the team. I think we deserved it. We believed we could score right up until the very end and we did, and I think it’s a deserved win.”It was another close-range strike from Naderi and he joked about this proficiency from distance. The Germany-born Czechia international said: “I’ve tried to shoot twice today from outside of the box and it didn’t go well.“So I went back inside the box. Maybe I should just stick to the easy ones! As I said, I’m just happy how it is right now and I’m going to try to stick to it.”Rangers – who will face the winners of Sunday’s semi-final between Hearts and Hibernian in the final – went into the game unbeaten in 10 and firm favourites.With five Aberdeen defenders missing through suspension or injury – Lewis Mayo, Mats Knoester, Dan Happe, Kristers Tobers and Chris Cadden – there was a makeshift element about their lineup, with a first start of the season for Nicky Devlin.McInnes, the Rangers manager who won the trophy with Aberdeen in 2014, raised eyebrows by dropping midfielder Dan Neil, with left-back Tuur Rommens starting and Penrice moving into midfield, and Badredine Bouanani starting in place of Djeidi Gassama.View image in fullscreenRyan Naderi diverts James Prentice’s shot past Marius Müller.Photograph: Kirk O’Rourke/Rangers FC/ShutterstockThere was more readjustment for Aberdeen when Emmanuel Gyamfi injured himself trying to tackle Kim Min-su and was replaced by Stuart Armstrong.In the 23rd minute, the Rangers defence parted and Nesta Guinness-Walker drove through the gap, forcing goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to save. Aberdeen captain Kevin Nisbet glanced a header wide of the goal before Naderi hooked an effort over the crossbar.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuick GuideScottish Premiership roundup: Saints dedicate draw to dismissed StewardShowSimo Valakari dedicatedSt Johnstone’s battling 2-2 draw atKilmarnockto the goalkeeper Toby Steward, who was dismissed in the 14th minute (pictured) after misjudging a long ball and handling outside his penalty area. Saints then twice fell behind to Cathal McCarthy and Djenairo Daniels, but equalised both times with goals from Danny Schmidt and Joel Cotterill to capture an unlikely point. The substitute goalkeeper Ross Sinclair, who came on at the expense of Taylor Steven, also made multiple second-half saves to help Saints move up to seventh.Valakari, the St Johnstone manager, said: “Toby has held his hands up and said: ‘I am sorry, boys, for what I did.’ But our team did it for Toby, the boys did it for Taylor, who I needed to take out straight away.“We are all here playing for each other. We have got each other’s backs when things happen. That tells me my players are ready to accept any responsibility. Early red card, with Toby that’s my tactical choice. I ask my keeper to play very high, like a sweeper-keeper for those long balls. In those moments, for a year, Toby has been fantastic in clearing the ball, reading the ball. It’s a thin line, a little outside the box, that can happen.”Alfred Johansson admitted he was left to sweat asMotherwellbroke a seven-game winless run with a 1-0 win overSt Mirren. Lukas Fadinger rattled home a penalty eight minutes from time to relieve some pressure on the Swede as the Fir Park side climbed into eighth.Johansson was adamant his team were well worthy of a result, which brought welcome relief to both him and his players. He said: “Even more than relief, I felt good, happy, joy, determination. This group has done really well lately and I think it’s very well deserved to get the victory and have at least four points from these last two games. It’s important to build on it, the most important thing today is that we didn’t give away easy goals or big chances at all."Press AssociationPhotograph: Andy Buchanan/Shutterstock EditorialWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Just before the break Aberdeen goalkeeper Marius Müller parried a low drive from Bouanani to safety, then Naderi headed a cross from stand-in captain Nico Raskin just over before Kim slashed a drive wide.As the game became stretched, Pandur saved a deflected Kevin Nesbit drive then Müller blocked a shot from Kim before Rangers striker Kevin Kelsy somehow managed to head a pinpoint delivery from Bouanani past a post from six yards.Müller’s foot blocked another effort from Bouanani and beat away a Raskin volley as the Aberdeen box came under siege. On a rare break, Nesbit’s shot was deflected wide and from the corner the Aberdeen striker hooked over the bar.Aberdeen finally succumbed when Bouanani knocked the ball back to Penrice and he fired towards goal, with Naderi stepping in to beat Müller from close range.Explore more on these topicsScottish League CupRangersAberdeenmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Julio Enciso strikes again to earn Ipswich a point against Hull | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Julio Enciso rescued Ipswich, as he did last week against Nottingham Forest, to earn his side a 2-2 draw at Hull
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Julio Enciso rescued Ipswich, as he did last week against Nottingham Forest, to earn his side a 2-2 draw at Hull
Content: Julio Enciso scores the leveller from just outside the area after Ipswich had led then fallen 2-1 behind.Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJulio Enciso scores the leveller from just outside the area after Ipswich had led then fallen 2-1 behind.Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueJulio Enciso strikes again to earn Ipswich a point against HullPress AssociationSat 31 Oct 2026 13.21 EDTLast modified on Sat 31 Oct 2026 18.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHull maintained their unbeaten home record, but their winless run stretched to eight games after Julio Enciso earned Ipswich a draw at the MKM Stadium.Ipswich had the lion’s share of possession in the first half, cutting through Hull’s defence repeatedly and Nobel Mendy and Konstantinos Tzolakis were unable to prevent Florentino Luis’s 22nd-minute opener as he sliced through on the right unhindered.After 37 minutes, the visitors appeared to have doubled their lead as Enciso headed in from a corner, but the effort was disallowed for a foul on Oli McBurnie.Sakamoto sparks Coventry win to keep 10-man Sunderland rock-bottomRead moreHull upped their game after the break and after 58 minutes Tim Iroegbunam raced down the right and fired home the equaliser.The pattern of the game changed entirely and 10 minutes later McBurnie slammed the ball beyond Christian Walton from a free-kick to giveHull the lead.But it lasted only six minutes as Enciso worked his way through Hull’s backline to produce a stylish leveller from just outside the area. It followed his equaliser last week that earned his sidea 1-1 draw against Nottingham Forest.“We were excellent, the better side for almost all of it,” said the Ipswich manager, Gary O’Neil. “There’s disappointment that it doesn’t get us three [points], but a point on the road in thePremier Leagueis still something.“There was a lot of promise that we were much better than them in their own stadium. That takes some doing, they’re a good side and they’ve been doing well. You have to give them credit, they’ve done this against everybody.“They don’t dominate the game, they don’t batter your goal, but if you make a mistake they will capitalise on it and that was the case today.”After dominating possession early on Ipswich were rewarded with Florentino slipping past Mendy to leave Tzolakis with no chance as the ball flew past him and into the right corner.View image in fullscreenOli McBurnie celebrates after putting Hull 2-1 ahead against Ipswich.Photograph: Dave Lofthouse/Action Plus/ShutterstockJust over 10 minutes later the visitors threatened again, this time turning a corner, but it was chalked off as the referee, Thomas Kirk, adjudged McBurnie had been fouled by Abdul Fatawu.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAfter the break, Ipswich continued to cause Hull problems, with Emersonn hitting the side-netting, having worked his way neatly through Hull’s back four. At the other end Walton was tested by a Lewie Coyle cross.The hosts were pressing and the equaliser arrived when Iroegbunam was played through in space by a fine McBurnie pass and fired home.The home side continued to look increasingly threatening, with Coyle going close with a shot that went wide before McBurnie stuck a 68th-minute free-kick through the wall.Hull could not keep hold of the lead, however, and Enciso picked his way through the defence to fire home impressively and make it 2-2.“We should have controlled the last 20 minutes better because Enciso scored an excellent goal, but still we could have defended it,” said the Hull manager, Sergej Jakirovic. “But if you cannot win, at least don’t lose. I know we are waiting now for almost two months for a win, but I am still positive.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueHull CityIpswich Townmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: ‘We need to be better’: Manchester United’s Olid demands progress after Everton draw | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Manchester United were held to a 0-0 draw at Goodison Park by Everton in the Women’s Super League
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Manchester United were held to a 0-0 draw at Goodison Park by Everton in the Women’s Super League
Content: Manchester United’s Andrea Medina has a close-range effort saved by Courtney Brosnan of Everton.Photograph: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenManchester United’s Andrea Medina has a close-range effort saved by Courtney Brosnan of Everton.Photograph: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty ImagesWomen's Super League‘We need to be better’: Manchester United’s Olid demands progress after Everton drawTom Garryat Goodison ParkSat 31 Oct 2026 10.59 EDTLast modified on Sat 31 Oct 2026 18.06 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA group of well-choreographed, fancy-dress-wearing school-age dancers fully embraced the Halloween spirit on Saturday as they boogied to one of Michael Jackson’s greatest hits at half-time here. Alas, the match itself was no thriller.For Manchester United, the only scary thing about this game was how little they tested Courtney Brosnan in Everton’s goal in the first 75 minutes as they demonstrated their lack of creativity.Putellas provides mindset change as London City bid to upstage championsRead moreBrosnan did well to save from Elisabeth Terland’s strike, as United grew into the game late on and began to apply some pressure, but this was a fixture worthy of finishing goalless or – as Sky Sports put it – ghoul-less.Terland has scored five Women’s Super League goals against Everton, but Brosnan was equal to her close-range shot after Jess Park’s through ball.“It was not a good performance, but we aren’t always going to perform amazing or good,” said the Manchester United head coach, Eva Olid. “But it’s [about] always finding a way to win and today we didn’t.“We need to be better. Out of possession, we were late, jumping late, to the individual duels, and in-possession we missed that creativity or connections we were having in the last matches.”Everton, who are winless in all 15 WSL meetings with United, will be the happier with the point, and their encouraging performance, but they missed the opportunity to climb above their opponents into fourth and might wish they could have converted some of their good midfield play.Their former Manchester United full-back Hannah Blundell hooked a dangerous effort, left-footed, towards the top corner in the first half, but her shot was saved by Phallon Tullis-Joyce, who also held on to shots – directed straight at her – from Ornella Vignola either side of the break.Rosa van Gool and Yuka Momiki were combining well for Everton in midfield to frustrate United. United had won away at Everton in the past four seasons, but they were second best in the first half and unable to break the deadlock in the closing stages, despite making improvements after Simi Awujo came on.United have been on a positive run, winning three and drawing one of their previous four WSL matches, the derby against Manchester Citythrough a morale-boosting late equaliser, as well as enjoying a 100% record in the Players Cup, but they were stifled by an Everton side whose midfield kept the ball well.Olid, who took over from Marc Skinner in August, said: “After such a positive performance on Sunday [against City] there is always that question – [are we] going to keep that standard or are we going to go a little down, like a hangover after that good match? I expected we would be better than we were. If this has to happen for us to learn and improve, we are going to do that.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionA Park effort sailed high over the bar, after an Andrea Medina shot was blocked inside the Everton area, but otherwise there was relatively little to note of United’s first hour, from an attacking perspective.This was Everton’s first draw of the league campaign, after three wins and four defeats, and they climbed above Arsenal – who play on Sunday – into sixth. They remain two points behind United, as Scott Phelan continues to oversee a steady – if unspectacular – spell in charge.The Everton head coach said: “In the first half, I thought we were competitive, we showed some good bits with the ball. We just probably lacked a little bit of end product and belief in our game to finish the good passages of play we had. Second half, not so much, but it did highlight the togetherness of the team and the defensive organisation.”His team certainly did look defensively well-organised. All they were really lacking was a top-quality focal point in attack, in a wretched game that did little to generate suspense.PosTeamPGDPts1Chelsea Women717192Man City Women711193London City Lionesses711164Man Utd Women8-2125Tottenham Hotspur Women73106Everton Women8-2107Arsenal Women7-198Aston Villa Women7-599Brighton & Hove Albion Women73810Liverpool FC Women72811Birmingham City Women7-4612West Ham Women7-8613Crystal Palace Women7-9614Charlton Women7-160Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueEverton WomenManchester United WomenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: If Mikel Arteta’s dossier is part of a deliberate strategy, it is a dangerous one for Arsenal | Mikel Arteta | The Guardian
description: The Arsenal manager is not yet in Alex Ferguson and José Mourinho’s league, but his conspiracy theories are reaching new levels
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: The Arsenal manager is not yet in Alex Ferguson and José Mourinho’s league, but his conspiracy theories are reaching new levels
Content: Mikel Arteta, booked here against Sunderland, received his second yellow card of the season for leaving the technical area against Everton.Photograph: Ian Hodgson/APView image in fullscreenMikel Arteta, booked here against Sunderland, received his second yellow card of the season for leaving the technical area against Everton.Photograph: Ian Hodgson/APInside footballMikel ArtetaIf Mikel Arteta’s dossier is part of a deliberate strategy, it is a dangerous one for ArsenalJonathan WilsonThe manager is not yet in Alex Ferguson and José Mourinho’s league, but his conspiracy theories have reached new levelsSat 31 Oct 2026 16.00 EDTLast modified on Sat 31 Oct 2026 16.01 EDTShareEnglish football loves the word “dossier”. It doesn’t love dossiers themselves, of course; they’re for nerds – unless, that is, they’re a “secret dossier”, which have a thrilling redolence of spy dramas, invisible ink and dead drops. Non-secret dossiers, though, are inherently risible: call something a “dossier” in English football and you’re immediately signalling: this is absurd poindextering. Dossiers were preposterous when Don Revie was – imagine the pretension! – drawing up scouting reports on opposing players, and they are preposterous today asMikel Artetacollates images of rival managers stepping outside their technical area.Arteta, it should be said, did not use the word “dossier”; rather it was swiftly applied to what he had called “a massive storage of images”. DuringArsenal’s 2-0 win against Evertonlast Saturday, he received his second booking of the season for leaving his technical area. This, it turns out, is another part of the vast conspiracy against Arsenal. Yes, Arteta accepted, he left his technical area (44 times before being booked, according to the former referee Graham Scott), but other managers do it too. “There are managers who have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes [they] leave the touchline – no yellows,” he said. “I am clipping all of that … so if somebody comes to me I can say: ‘I am not in the record yet.’ Somebody else has the record so let’s see. Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers.”‘We are not in Disneyland’: Arteta warns Dowman of Arsenal’s demandsRead moreThere are two ways of looking at this. Perhaps it’s genuine. Perhaps Arteta really is a ludicrous Pooterish figure, counting the misdemeanours of others, the worst kind of neighbourhood watch curtain-twitcher who happens also to have been cursed with a persecution complex: “I got a fine because my parking permit was partially obscured, but Mr Emery at No 17 has been six inches out of his bay on at least three occasions this month and … nothing.” Or perhaps he really is an inveterate snitch, glorying in telling on his peers: “Please, Miss! Miss, Daniel’s been chewing gum again, Miss.”Or, perhaps awed by the misguided defiance of Manchester City fans after their club was found to have perpetrated the greatest act of cheating in English sporting history, he is trying to persuade his base that everybody is againstArsenalto generate a siege mentality. Declan Rice mystifyingly got away with kicking Malick Yalcouyé off the ball against Brighton, but it’s important to remember that Arsenal remain the real victims here.The history of mind games in football is long and storied. Before the 1939 FA Cup final, for instance, Major Frank Buckley, the flamboyant manager of Wolves, claimed to have injected his players with “animal secretions”. A French surgeon, Serge Voronoff, had begun transplanting tissue from monkey testicles on to human testicles as an anti-ageing treatment, and it was widely believed that it was this monkey gland treatment that Buckley was employing. In fact, he almost certainly gave his players nothing stronger than vitamins but the idea was that Wolves’ morale would be boosted, while their opponents in the final, Portsmouth, would be intimidated by the prospect of taking on players juiced up on simian fluids. It didn’t work, Portsmouth winning 4-1 despite finishing 15 places below Wolves in the table, but the logic is familiar.The monkey glands were relatively benign, little more than a publicity stunt, but it’s easy for attempts at psychological manipulation to take on a darker aspect. Before Inter played Liverpool in the second leg of the 1965 European Cup semi-final, for instance, their manager, Helenio Herrera, had 100,000 leaflets distributed claiming that at the end of the first leg at Anfield, Liverpool fans had sung “Go home, Italians” to the tune of “Santa Lucia” which supposedly was intended “to deride us and make us feel we are just a race of cheap mandolin players”. Suitably enraged, Inter fans ensured San Siro seethed with fury, which perhaps encouraged some questionable refereeing decisions (although it probably wasn’t the only factor) as Liverpool lost 3-0 and went out 4-3 on aggregate.Alex Ferguson was a master of the art, while José Mourinho openly acknowledged that the next game begins in the post-match press conference for the previous one. Mourinho, in particular, often crossed the line of professional decency. Arteta, clearly, is not at that level, at least not yet, but if his dossier is part of a deliberate strategy it is a dangerous one.View image in fullscreenArsenal fans, more so after Max Dowman’s red card at Fleetwood, remain convinced that referees have been machinating against them for years.Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty ImagesArteta’s conspiracy theory is likely to find fertile ground among certain online Arsenal fans, who remain convinced that referees have been machinating against them for years. Even on Tuesday there were those who leaped to thedefence of Max Dowmanafter he had been sent off for thrusting a knee towards Harrison Neal’s chest, even though Arteta himself appeared furious with the16-year-old’s petulance. Why, ran the argument, had Cole Palmer not been shown a straight red for retaliating against Mateus Fernandes in Chelsea’s defeat by Tottenham on Saturday? Dowman went with his knee and Palmer with his belly, which is perhaps enough to explain the discrepancy, but even if it isn’t, so what? If you don’t want to be punished, don’t go thrusting knees or bellies or anything at opponents, no matter how bad a foul they’ve just committed.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIt’s not only that football is groaning under the weight of the paranoia of various fan groups, each adamant that Pro Ref is acting with the rosicrucians, the Masons, the mob, Opus Dei and the Cubans to deny their club a spot in the Europa League, a distraction that deflects from the game’s true crisis: its descent from an endeavour in which sporting merit and integrity are paramount into a grimly capitalistic vehicle to make very rich and powerful people even richer and more powerful.It’s also dangerous because a mood of insecurity, of being convinced everything is against you, is not conducive to winning league titles – as Arsenal know. In 2024-25, their title bid was undermined by their early-season ill discipline, each red card greeted not with the resilience of champions but with bleating about how it wasn’t really their fault and everybody was picking on them, including the injury gods.Abdicating responsibility rarely helps, snitches seldom prosper and, in English football, dossiers are always a bad idea.Explore more on these topicsMikel ArtetaInside footballArsenalcommentShareReuse this content

title: Championship roundup: Pressure grows on Nuno as West Ham beaten at home | Championship | The Guardian
description: Nuno Espirito Santo is facing mounting pressure after West Brom’s stylish 3-1 win at the London Stadium left West Ham, the Championship promotion favourites, six points off the pace in eighth place
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Nuno Espirito Santo is facing mounting pressure after West Brom’s stylish 3-1 win at the London Stadium left West Ham, the Championship promotion favourites, six points off the pace in eighth place
Content: Nuno Espírito Santo reacts during West Ham’s defeat to West Brom.Photograph: Paul Marriott/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenNuno Espírito Santo reacts during West Ham’s defeat to West Brom.Photograph: Paul Marriott/ShutterstockChampionshipChampionship roundup: Pressure grows on Nuno as West Ham beaten at homeHammers fans angry after West Brom seal 3-1 victorySwansea win 4-0; Middlesbrough cruise against CharltonPress AssociationSat 31 Oct 2026 13.39 EDTFirst published on Sat 31 Oct 2026 11.08 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNuno Espirito Santo is facing mounting pressure afterWest Brom’sstylish 3-1 win at the London Stadium leftWest Ham, theChampionshippromotion favourites, six points off the pace in eighth place.A second consecutive home defeat contained few saving graces for Nuno, who faced the wrath of fans on the final whistle. Albion, slick and measured, moved into the top four with their 3,000 travelling fans revelling in the discomfort of Nuno, once manager of arch-rivals Wolves.Manchester United crisis deepens with Chelsea defeat and Martínez red cardRead moreAfter falling behind in nine of their previous 15 games, West Ham conceded first again on 20 minutes, with the unmarked midfielder Felix Horn Myhre firing home from point-blank range.West Ham levelled when a Jarrod Bowen shot deflected in off Callum Styles, but within three minutes of the restart Albion were back in front. Jimmy-Jay Morgan1 struck his fourth goal of the season from the corner of the six-yard box.Within two minutes of Walker-Peters limping off with a thigh injury, and with Nuno using up all his five substitutes, Price’s corner was only half-cleared to Styles and his fierce, deflected shot made it three.Asked about visiting fans’ taunts that he would be “sacked in the morning”, Nuno said: “This is the reality: we can only change this if we win games. There is pressure every day. We have conceded six goals at home in two games and we have to fix it. The idea and the approach is to try and score first. That is the objective of any team and it’s our responsibility to change it.”View image in fullscreenWest Ham fans leave early during their defeat to West Brom.Photograph: Martin Dalton/ShutterstockThe in-form Will Lankshear scored twice asMiddlesbroughmaintained their position at the top with a comprehensive 3-0 victory overCharltonat the Riverside. Sebastian Berhalter opened the scoring in the 12th minute before Lankshear netted twice to take his tally to 15 in all competitions.Quick GuideLeague One roundup: Huddersfield thump BradfordShowAn overhead kick from Joe Low opened the scoring as  League One leadersHuddersfieldswept aside 10-manBradford3-0 in the West Yorkshire derby. Huddersfield went in front after four minutes and two goals in six minutes at the start of the second half from Derensili Sanches Fernandes and Joe Taylor killed off the contest at Valley Parade. The Bradford captain, Antoni Sarcevic, was sent off with a second yellow card in the 70th minute.Jack Diamond and Ethan Ennis ensured second-placedStockportkept pace in a 2-1 comeback overAFC Wimbledonat Edgeley Park after Jayden Stockley broke the deadlock for the visitors in the 47th minute. Third-placedOxfordandBarnsleyfinished with 10 men in their 1-1 draw. Hosts Barnsley were left short-handed for the majority of the contest after Jack Shepherd was sent off in the ninth minute. Vimal Yoganathan’s 32nd-minute opener for Barnsley was cancelled out by Mark Harris on the hour, and the Us went down to 10 men after their goalkeeper, Jamie Cumming, was sent off with two minutes remaining in normal time.LutonbeatPeterborough2-0,Plymouthplayed out a goalless draw withReading,Leicestersplit the points in a 2-2 draw withStevenageandLeyton OrientbeatCambridge3-0.Notts Countywere 2-0 victors atMansfield,MK DonsdrubbedDoncaster6-1,Wycombewon 2-0 againstBurtonandWiganbeatBromley3-2.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Swanseaprovided the perfect response to last Saturday’s hammering at QPR by beatingBlackburn4-0. The hosts were three goals to the good by half-time thanks to Stephen Eustáquio, Joseph Opoki and Filip Lissah, with the Scotland international striker Ross Stewart scoring his first goal for the Swans on the hour mark to complete the rout. Tony Mowbray’s Rovers had arrived in Wales having won four of their previous six games, including last week’s 2-0 home victory overWrexham, but were blown away in the first half.View image in fullscreenRoss Stewart celebrates scoring Swansea’s fourth against Blackburn.Photograph: Gareth Everett/Huw Evans/ShutterstockHeaded goals from Fer Lopez, Adam Armstrong and Ladislav Krejci helpedWolvesbeatCardiff3-0 at Molineux. Wolves gave themselves the platform for victory by scoring twice in the first 15 minutes and made it four games unbeaten and back-to-back wins without conceding, ending Cardiff’s three-match unbeaten run.Cameron Bragg scored his first Championship goal asSouthamptonmade it 17 home league matches without losing with a 4-1 victory overQPR. Kuryu Matsuki, Keven Schlotterbeck and Welington also got on the scoresheet as Saints stayed fifth and kept pace with the leaders.Two-goal August Priske was praised by his manager, Chris Davies, after the recalled Danish striker helpedBirminghambeatLincoln3-1 at the ProAmpac Stadium. He scored either side of the break to take his season tally to seven, with Alex Cochrane securing the win after the Imps substitute Tom Bayliss had reduced the deficit.“He gave us a real focal point, with his size and his strength,” said Davies. “He’s very mature for his age and he has all the tools, the temperament, the technical skills, the physicality and again he just needs to keep hungry, keep pushing.”Mark Robins saluted his on-songStokeside but admitted they could have been “more clinical” despite putting bottom sidePrestonto the sword with a comfortable 2-0 victory. Goals from Ben Wilmot and Jack McGlynn did the damage as Stoke claimed a seventh victory in their past 10 league games.Quick GuideLeague Two: Aimson stunner seals it for SalfordShowWill Aimson scored a spectacular long-range goal as top-of-the-leagueSalfordbattled to a 2-1 win over in-formExeter. The 32-year-old centre-back opened his Salford account in style two minutes from time after Luke Garbutt had cancelled out Sonny Cox’s first-half opener for the Grecians.BarnetandCrewedrew 1-1, as didAccringtonandNorthampton, andTranmerecame from behind to secure their first home win since early September with an impressive 3-1 victory overCheltenhamat Prenton Park. A double from Dylan Jones and a stunning strike from Charlie Whitaker before the break overturned Charlie McCann’s early opener to give Rovers all three points.Fleetwoodfollowed their Carabao Cup win overArsenalwith a 3-1 victory overBristol Roversat Highbury. Matt Lawlor’s side picked up the three points thanks to goals from Aaron Loupalo-Bi, Rhys Bennett and Josh Roberston.Colchesterwere dealt a 3-1 defeat byWalsall,GrimsbybeatYork5-2,Swindonsecured a 2-1 victory overRotherham,Gillinghamwon 2-1 atShrewsbury,Port ValebeatRochdale4-2, andOldhamfell 1-0 toCrawley.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Fabio Celestini’s tenure asBurnleyhead coach began with a 0-0 draw againstPortsmouthat Turf Moor as the Clarets failed to capitalise on their first-half advantage. The Swiss manager, who celebrated his 51st birthday on Saturday, saw his side create a host of chances before the break, but a lack of clinical finishing ultimately cost them.Kyrell Lisbie scored twice in the early stages asMillwalleased to a 4-1 victory against strugglingDerbyat The Den. The Lions scored three goals in the first 17 minutes to cruise to their second win in eight league games. It was another worrying afternoon for the Rams, though, who were never in the contest and remain second from bottom, four points from safety, and without a win in nine games.Bristol Citycame from behind to stunBolton3-2 with an added-time Scott Twine winner. The visitors trailed 2-1 with six minutes of normal time remaining, but Sam Bell levelled before fellow substitute Twine ensured their manager, Michael Skubala, celebrated his 44th birthday with three points. City’s win was their first in five games while Bolton have now gone six weeks since their last success at home.View image in fullscreenAnthony Musaba celebrates after equalising against Watford.Photograph: MB Media/Getty ImagesAlessio Dionisi hit out at his players afterWatfordsurrendered a two-goal half-time lead to lose 3-2 atNorwich, increasing the pressure on his position.Watfordlooked well placed to take the points after Myron Boadu opened his account for the club with a well-taken double, but Norwich were a different side in the second half, and never looked back after Ben Chrisene had pulled one back in the 54th minute. Anthony Musaba raced through down the right to level the scores after 62 minutes and nine minutes later it was 3-2 as Paris Maghoma fired home.“I am furious,” said Dionisi. “It is difficult to explain the difference between the first and second half. Football is crazy, I know that, but to lose a game like that – it’s impossible. There were nearly 1,300 Watford fans here today and I would like to be saying thank you for their support rather than saying sorry, again.”On Friday, Ben Brereton Díaz’s first goal of the season sealed a deserved 1-0 win forSheffield UnitedagainstWrexhamat Bramall Lane. The Chile forward, in his third spell on loan with the Blades, struck the only goal in the first half.Explore more on these topicsChampionshipLincoln CityBirmingham CityNorwich CityWatfordStoke CityPreston North EndnewsShareReuse this content

title: Is AI your new wingman? How chatbots are transforming dating | Dating | The Guardian
description: Almost 40% of British singles are using AI for romantic advice, from writing messages to assessing potential partners
Author: George Francis Lee
Headline: Almost 40% of British singles are using AI for romantic advice, from writing messages to assessing potential partners
Content: Illustration: Anaïs Mims/Guardian DesignView image in fullscreenIllustration: Anaïs Mims/Guardian DesignDatingIs AI your new wingman? How chatbots are transforming datingAlmost 40% of British singles have used AI for romantic advice, from writing messages to assessing potential partnersGeorge Francis LeeandDan MilmoSat 31 Oct 2026 08.00 EDTLast modified on Sat 31 Oct 2026 08.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAfter Sam’s ex joked that her sister found him ugly, he turned to AI. Google Gemini had a look at the photo and politely disagreed. AI has been his wingman ever since, aiding his dating life by giving pep talks and vetting his messages.The 27-year-old from Stoke-on-Trent is not the only AI-assisted romantic – a survey of 3,000 British singles published this month by Match Group, the owner of theTinderand Hinge platforms, found 39% had used AI in their dating lives.Relying on AI is bad, Sam tells the Guardian, adding he would rather begin dating in person, but there is a “paradigm shift in dating that’s occurring, which is really odd, where everything is expected to start online”.The proportion of AI use in dating is even higher for younger generations, rising to 66% for members of gen Z (people born in the mid 1990s to early 2010s), and 53% of millennials (those born in the early 1980s to mid-90s).Sam says pressure to make a good impression on dating apps means a misunderstood message could risk him losing out on dates. “Online dating … as a guy it’s a bit of a ghost town,” he says. “Rather than saying: ‘Hey, how’s your weekend going?’ it’s thinking about what I can pick up that might get a response.”The most common use of AI across all cohorts, according to Match, is to get advice about someone they are talking to, plan date ideas, practise conversations, write a dating profile or messages, and vet whether profiles or photos are genuine. Using AI to alter a photo is a no-no for the majority of singles, the survey says.View image in fullscreenSome singles are turning to AI to navigate online dating, using chatbots to plan dates and check whether profiles are genuine.Photograph: oatawa/Getty Images/iStockphotoA single mother from New Zealand, who asked to remain anonymous, says she has used AI as a dating mentor. “I did not really date before I met my ex-husband … with ChatGPT I set it up to coach me to become more secure – to not panic about any delay in messaging, to not rush into anything,” she says.One man from Melbourne, Australia, who began dating after his 20-year marriage ended, says AI made finding his current partner faster by assessing people he “matched” with and testing his responses. “It was getting [to be] quite a lot of work, like all the chats and the profiles. So I thought: ‘How can I use AI just to sort of speed it up a little bit?’” he says.The 51-year-old adds that the chatbot he was using helped him think twice about profiles he’d overlooked. “[With] my current partner, it was really aggressive with me saying that: ‘Nah, she’s your vibe, she just takes shit photos.’ And then I meet her at a cafe and she’s absolutely drop-dead gorgeous,” he says.When he told his partner he had used AI in their exchanges, she also admitted to using Anthropic’s Claude chatbot to analyse his responses. He says she joked that the “two Claudes were probably just chatting away behind the scenes”. It is a risky admission, though – about a third of UK singles said they would end a date if they found out AI had been used to write a potential paramour’s messages.But, while a few singles like to discuss how their date went with a chatbot (7%), far more prefer a group chat (29%) or their parents (20%), according to the Match survey. “Maybe our friends are becoming more distant because of technology, a little more hands off, compared to the generation before us [who] would get together in their flat or the pub and just absolutely dish the dirt,” says Dec, 31, from London, who uses ChatGPT as a “sounding board” when chatting with single men.Dec says he uploaded his dating conversations to ChatGPT and gave it prompts such as: “Tell me what you think the red flags there are”, and: “What does this connection look like?”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toTechScapeA weekly dive in to how technology is shaping our livesEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAlthough deploying the chatbot charmer led to a number of dates, Dec worries that his “brain feels like it’s rotting because everything’s just offloaded to AI now”. He adds: “We all know it’s going to be a bit of a yes man sometimes.”View image in fullscreenAbout a third of British singles say they would end a date if they discovered the other person had used AI to write their messages.Photograph: Maskot/Getty ImagesThe Match survey also hinted at a robotic romantic future where autonomous AIs do people’s dating work for them. More than a quarter of respondents liked the idea of two people’s assistants talking to each other and reporting back before the people speak – even if a majority think the idea is “unacceptable”. Match’s head of trust and safety, Yoel Roth, says the company is taking a “hard stance” against bot-to-bot dating.“In a world where people say that they’re more alienated than ever, are hungrier for connection than ever, we don’t get closer to that goal of human connection by having robots talk to each other,” he says.Sam agrees that AI can only enhance his prospects by so much: “If I replace my humour with AI I think I’ve died as a person.”Explore more on these topicsDatingAI (artificial intelligence)ChatbotsTinderComputingfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: ‘Apologies for any confusion!’: how to write the perfect passive-aggressive email | Email | The Guardian
description: In a survey, ‘just to be clear’ came out as the most loathed phrase. But I think I can do better
Author: Emma Beddington
Headline: In a survey, ‘just to be clear’ came out as the most loathed phrase. But I think I can do better
Content: ‘I think we’d all be happier taking a deep breath.’Photograph: Posed by model; Francesco Carta fotografo/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreen‘I think we’d all be happier taking a deep breath.’Photograph: Posed by model; Francesco Carta fotografo/Getty ImagesEmail‘Apologies for any confusion!’: how to write the perfect passive-aggressive emailIn a survey, ‘just to be clear’ came out as the most loathed phrase. But I think I can do betterEmma BeddingtonSat 31 Oct 2026 01.00 EDTLast modified on Sat 31 Oct 2026 01.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAnew contender for the most passive-aggressive email phrase has emerged. “Just to be clear” was chosen by 52% of desk jockeys in a survey by email verification company ZeroBounce, closely followed by the perennial pass-ag fave, “per my last email” (40%), which tied with the identical-in-intent “as previously discussed”. Further down the list came “for future reference” and “kindly note”.If you ask me, these all verge onactualaggressive. Imagine saying “just to be clear” out loud to another person: that’s a conversational poke in the ribs, isn’t it? It’s the kind of thing you unleash 10 minutes into an ill-tempered wrangle with your home insurance company about inflated renewal premiums. “Kindly note” is even worse – it’s a phrase from an angry message on the office kitchen wall about microwave abuse.No, we can do better than that, or at least I – a person whose own spouse frequently describes her as unpleasantly passive-aggressive – can. Let me explain: an exchange of professional passive-aggressive emails is a ritual as intricately coded as a Belle Epoque duel and it demands the appearance of great politeness. Your message needs to read, on its surface, as exquisitely helpful and friendly, while leaving every cc and bcc on the thread in no doubt as to it what it really is: an epistolary shanking.A good pass-agg email starts with a simulacrum of warmth and gratitude. I can usually generate the appearance of warmth by harnessing the dizzying rush of anger generated by whatever stupid message has prompted me to press “reply all”. “Hi X!” I usually start perkily, then I pause to hold up both middle fingers to the screen. Next comes gratitude: “Great to hear from you,” (it wasn’t) “and thank you so much for your message”. Thanks, that is, for giving me a chance to show everyone you’re out of line. I say “everyone”, because I like to deploy a cc on this kind of email.I follow this Trojan Shetland pony of an intro with a selection of my preferred zingers:“My understanding was … apologies if this was incorrect?”I understood perfectly. I am correct. I am sorry for nothing. The question mark is a mere disingenuous flourish.“As agreed,”The import of this little phrase is clear: I have kept the receipts and I want you to know that. This email will be followed near-instantaneously by a second email, forwarding the evidence that I am right. The body of that second email will just read “FYI”, which is passive-aggressive for “checkmate, loser”.“Apologies for any confusion”or“apologies if this was unclear”It, and I, was entirely clear. I am only sorry you are a dolt. Some pass-ag practitioners drop in a bland, smiling emoji here, but I am a purist.Hope this helps!I hope this leaves you seething with the same fury your message inspired in me.“No response required”By saying I don’t expect you to respond it will make you look petty when you do; it also subtly implies you’ve already gone home. Your move.Warm regards,Warm like the fires of hell.Still, as much as I get satisfaction from the perfect turn of passive-aggressive phrase, I always realise later that it’s a hollow pleasure. What am I doing fighting, albeit with elegant restraint, a fellow worker when the real enemy is capitalism? Why are we emailing at all when we could be contemplating the beauty of a sunset, shoulder to shoulder? For future reference: I think we’d all be happier taking a deep breath, pressing backspace, and walking away.Explore more on these topicsEmailWork & careersfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Hear me out: maybe Norway should give Melania Trump the Nobel peace prize | Arwa Mahdawi | The Guardian
description: The first lady has been praised for ‘singlehandedly’ brokering a ceasefire in a Ukrainian city – though she might have had some help
Author: Arwa Mahdawi
Headline: The first lady has been praised for ‘singlehandedly’ brokering a ceasefire in a Ukrainian city – though she might have had some help
Content: ‘If Melania can do something about her husband, I’m crowning her Michigan’s Woman of the Year.’Photograph: Aaron Schwartz-Pool/CNP/ShutterstockView image in fullscreen‘If Melania can do something about her husband, I’m crowning her Michigan’s Woman of the Year.’Photograph: Aaron Schwartz-Pool/CNP/ShutterstockThe Week in PatriarchyMelania TrumpHear me out: maybe Norway should give Melania Trump the Nobel peace prizeArwa MahdawiThe first lady has been praised for ‘singlehandedly’ brokering a ceasefire in a Ukrainian city – though she might have had some helpSat 31 Oct 2026 08.00 EDTLast modified on Sat 31 Oct 2026 08.02 EDTShareHaters be damned: Donald Trump just keeps on winning. He won the inaugural Fifa peace prize last year and was presented with the completely real, totally not made-up “Man of the Century” award at arecent rally. The president has also spent thegreater part of a decadeclaiming he was once crowned Michigan’s Man of the Year: a fantastic achievement considering there is no such award and Trump has never lived in Michigan.But despite his manytrophies, there is one honour that has proved elusive: the Nobel peace prize. Trump holds a bit of a grudge about that, recently terming Norway a “shithouse country” for passing him over for the award. In response, thecountry’s tourism boardhighlighted some of its nicest public lavatories with the tagline: “Norway makes shit houses great again!”Speaking in my capacity as Philadelphia’s Woman of the Millennium, I’ve got a modest proposal for the people of Norway. The toilet gag was excellent, but if they want to do some top-tier trolling then I think next year’s Nobel peace prize needs to go toMelania Trump.Some people would be thrilled for their spouse to be in the spotlight, but I’m not sure that’s the case with Donald. Indeed, the president hassaid: “You can only have … one star in a family; it doesn’t work with two.” If Melania got Trump’s coveted Nobel peace prize, it could spark a war in the White House.But look, I’m not just suggesting the Norwegians honour Melania because it would raise Donald’s blood pressure. No, it seems Melania has become quite the diplomat. Last week, the White Houseannouncedthat the first lady had “successfully secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, localized to the city of Oleshky”.How on earth did she manage that? Apparently, Melania initiated discussions with Russia andUkraineand “aligned the parties on the agreement’s objectives, technical procedures, timing, processes, and terms, in her formal role as Exclusive Intermediary”.Whatever all that means, it seems to have worked: the ceasefire went into effect on Tuesday in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city, which has been enduring a worsening humanitarian crisis.On Friday, hundreds of people were evacuated from the frontline town and emergency supplies were brought in for people who needed to stay.Melania has been widely praised for brokering this ceasefire. Melania’s adviser has claimed she “singlehandedly” secured it, adding that no other first lady has everachievedwhat Melania just pulled off, and she is “completely revamping the role of first lady … [and] saving lives.”Perhaps. But if there is one thing that the Trumps are good at it, it is taking credit for other people’s work. So is the first lady really the great peacemaker that she’s making herself out to be?To be fair, Melania has done some good work vis-à-vis Ukraine and certainly seems to be better at peacemaking than Jared Kushner is, who has made huge sums of money while operating as one of Trump’stop diplomatic envoysto the Middle East. Last year, for example, Melaniawrote a letterto Vladimir Putin pleading for Ukrainian children seized by Russia to be returned to their families. Since then, her office has said she’s facilitatednumerous roundsof family reunification.However, despite the claim that Melania “singlehandedly” secured this ceasefire, it would appear she had a little help. Pope Leo XIV alsopersonally appealedto Putin about the situation in Oleshky in early October. It’s unclear whether he had more or less sway than the first lady had, but the pope is certainly being rather more modest about his involvement.So what’s next for Melania after her success in Oleshky? In an interview with Newsmax, her adviser Marc Beckman said Melaniamight help pavethe way to “durable, everlasting peace” in Ukraine and Russia as a whole.“She’s against war, she thinks it’s senseless … she wants to see peace all over the world,” Beckman added.Does she indeed? In that case she might want to have a word with the president, who started a very bloody war against Iran and who is currently trying to use US taxpayer money to send2,000lb bombs to Israel, a country accused of genocide.Forget the Nobel peace prize. If Melania can do something about her husband, I’m crowning her Michigan’s Woman of the Year.Bad news for US women trying to manage menopause symptomsLast November, the FDA announced that menopausal hormone therapy medications would no longer require a scary “black-box” label on them, which is the highest safety-related warning a medication can have. This reassured a lot of women about the treatment and caused a surge in demand. Supply didn’t keep up, and there’s been a shortage of estrogen patches in the USall yearbecause of an uptick in demand. Now Reutersreportsthat the shortage has spread beyond estrogen patches “with some injectable and vaginal estrogen products also in short supply”.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe Week in PatriarchyGet Arwa Mahdawi’s weekly recap of the most important stories on feminism and sexism and those fighting for equalityEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionDolores Huerta, labor leader and civil rights champion, dies aged 96Huerta co-founded the United Farm Workers union (UFW), which improved conditions for agricultural workers in the 1960s and 1970s. She isalso creditedwith coining the phrase “Sí, se puede!” (yes, we can), which was UFW’s slogan and then Barack Obama’s 2008 campaign rally cry.Kamala Harris advises Democrats not to impeach Trump if they win House and Senate“I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea,” Harris said in aMeidasTouch interview. “I was in the Senate for the last go-round, and the votes aren’t there.” In other words: don’t hold your breath that Trump will face immediate accountability if the Democrats dominate the midterms.Egypt continues crackdown on press freedom and fines editor Lina AttalahAttalah is the editor-in-chief of Madr Masar, an independent Egyptian news site that has frequently been critical of the Egyptian president Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi’s government. The government recently accused her of running a website without a license, detained her, andshut down Mada Masr. The crackdown “can only mean that Egypt’s security agencies are moving from years of harassing independent media to wiping them out completely”, one expert told the Guardian.The toxic legacy of body positivity“We are living through a strange time in the language around bodies,” writes Hannah Marriottin the Guardian. The body positivity era is over, but “much of its social training lingers.” Thanks to the GLP-1 boom, everyone is shrinking, but it’s taboo to talk about it. “What we’re left with is a world in which skinny bodies are lionized in fashion, culture and daily life, but to either admit a desire to conform, or express concern about it, feels socially verboten.”Queer romance is dead: Chrishell Stause and G Flip have broken upYou may be familiar with thisviral tweet: “I’m 50. All celebrity news looks like this: ‘Curtains for Zoosha? K-smog and Batboy caught flipping a grunt.’” I am still a mere 43, but I had my own curtains for Zoosha moment this week when I saw the headlines about G Flip, which I could have sworn was a watch. If you are similarly confused, Rebecca Shaw has anexplaineras to why some of the queer community are in mourning.Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnistExplore more on these topicsMelania TrumpThe Week in PatriarchyUkraineDonald TrumpWomenKamala HarrisDemocratsEgyptcommentShareReuse this content

title: Top Democrats are fighting a billionaire tax in California. Their voters are on the other side | Norman Solomon | The Guardian
description: The unprecedented measure has enormous potential nationwide. The clash exposes the party’s corporate-progressive divide
Author: Norman Solomon
Headline: The unprecedented measure has enormous potential nationwide. The clash exposes the party’s corporate-progressive divide
Content: ‘Gavin Newsom has lined up with Silicon Valley billionaires.’Photograph: Heather Diehl/APView image in fullscreen‘Gavin Newsom has lined up with Silicon Valley billionaires.’Photograph: Heather Diehl/APOpinionCaliforniaTop Democrats are fighting a billionaire tax in California. Their voters are on the other sideNorman SolomonThe unprecedented measure has enormous potential nationwide. The clash exposes the party’s corporate-progressive divideSat 31 Oct 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Sat 31 Oct 2026 07.10 EDTShareMidway through this summer, a high-qualitypollfound that Democrats in California were overwhelmingly in favor of the upcoming ballot measure for a one-time 5% tax on billionaire wealth.The ratio was more than 4 to 1. But the state’s most powerful Democrats – including the governor Gavin Newsom, his near-certain successor Xavier Becerra and the Los Angeles mayor Karen Bass – have lined up with Silicon Valley billionaires who’ve raised upward of$340mto defeat the initiative.While Newsom has led the charge against the measure, most Democratic leaders in the deep-blue state have opted to duck. California’s senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff have stayed mum on Proposition 40. The same is true of the former vice-president Kamala Harris and the former House speaker Nancy Pelosi.“Neither wants to alienate wealthy donors or their allies in labor by publicly opposing it,” the San Francisco Chroniclenotedin mid-October. “But their silence on such a high-profile measure is giving cover to the billionaires” fighting the measure.Nine-tenths of the billionaire tax revenue fromProposition 40would go to healthcare for Californians in need. As the New York Timesreportedthis month, “California stands to lose around $100 billion in federal Medicaid funding over the next five years, threatening healthcare coverage for millions of low-income residents, as well as the potential closure of hospitals and other facilities.”Democrats are at a huge crossroads in California governor’s race | Normon SolomonRead moreWith so much at stake in human terms, refusal to back Proposition 40 runs directly counter to standard rhetoric from Democratic politicians about standing up to the ultra-wealthy on behalf of the disadvantaged.The stance of Newsom and other Democratic heavyweights in the state puts them on the side of billionaires in ongoing class war. The effect is that party leaders are offering a kinder, gentler oligarchy as an alternative to the far more corrupt Trumpist version.Overall, a semblance of party unity has taken hold with the midterm elections looming. But clashes between corporateDemocratsand progressives will soon begin to escalate.The fact that the most prominent Democrats in the country’s most populous state are at loggerheads with the party’s grassroots on Prop 40 is a bad sign, but it’s hardly an anomaly.Every time a general election nears, party leaders fervently call for a huge turnout – but their disconnect from the party’s base discourages turnout. California’s billionaire tax proposal is unprecedented, but the response to it from Democratic party elites is part of a pattern that has undermined capacities to build populist momentum against Republicans, let alone advance progressive agendasfavored by voters.Now being vilified by an onslaught of attack ads, Proposition 40 might get buried under the avalanche of billionaire cash (withnearly halfcoming from the Google co-founder Sergey Brin).
